column1: # How each label reads as a scoring target: the machine-readable form of ROUND-<n>.md, used by
# `zoom-eval fit`. Edit it when the owner corrects a reading. Columns (tab-separated):
#   page     page number, or * for the paper
#   move     high | medium | low | none: confidence in the page's moved window (pages only);
#            high@10 etc.: the page should have page 10's crop as judged ("same as the rest")
#   keep     yes | no: the ink the ideal crop keeps must stay visible (pages only)
#   verdict  good | bad | -: the verdict a comment implies, where none was given (pages only)
#   zoom     affirmed | tighter | looser | -: what the label says about the paper's zoom
# Pages missing from this table read their labels plainly: a move of 8 pt or more is high
# confidence, a smaller one low, and a verdict as given. Each round's rows follow its
# ROUND-<n>.md, round 1 first. From round 2 on, small moves are deliberate nudges, so they are
# listed as high (or medium where the owner called the labels rough).
